stat.weight: less page code after leaving Tilda
sec.work.t: Seven projects, and every one's code is open
work.note: Every project below is a public repository — you can read the code before you pay.
sec.services.s: Pricing comes after I look at the task — before that it is guesswork.
svc.bots.d: A bot that does the work instead of showing a menu: takes requests, serves content, runs mailouts, and is managed from inside Telegram.
svc.bots.p1: Dialogue flow and an owner's admin panel
svc.bots.p3: Docker deployment on your own server
svc.bots.out: A working bot, its source code, and instructions to redeploy it
svc.sites.d: Pages are assembled from content by a generator instead of being drawn one by one. Changing a price or a line of text means one edit, not a hunt for copies.
svc.sites.p3: Deployment and automated checks in CI
svc.sites.out: A site on your domain and the repository it is built from
svc.auto.d: Work done by hand every day moves into a script: data collection, scheduled publishing, checks before release.
svc.auto.p1: The manual process broken down step by step
svc.auto.p3: Checks that catch a failure before you do
svc.auto.out: A process that runs itself and tells you when something breaks
sec.stack.s: Every name here appears in one of the projects below or in this site's own build.
sec.process.s: Five steps. The first one is free: if the job isn't worth doing, you'll hear it there.
step.audit.d: I look at what's already there, measure speed and weight, and say honestly whether the job is worth doing. Free.
step.arch.d: Data model, content sources, URL structure. Settled before the first line of markup.
step.build.d: Pages are generated from content, and a demo on a real address appears as the work goes.
step.ship.d: Content, figures, headings, and images are checked on every deploy. A wrong number never reaches a visitor.
step.hand.d: The repository moves to you. No subscription, no hostage hosting, no access you don't have.
footer.note: Built without frameworks or third-party libraries.
